title: Electricity Saver
subtitle: Occupancy-based air-conditioning and lighting control for an industrial cement plant
headline: 3,000 mesh-networked sensors automating air-conditioning and lighting across an industrial cement plant, saving 10–15% of the energy used
photoAlt: SciFlair occupancy sensor installed in an office ceiling next to a cassette air-conditioning unit
need: Air-conditioning and lights in the plant's offices were routinely left running in empty rooms, after hours and at weekends. In the region, air-conditioning can account for more than half of a building's electricity use.

The client needed unoccupied areas switched off automatically, without altering the existing air-conditioning units or wiring, with the manual switches staying in charge and the lights failing safe if power or the system was lost.
role: SciFlair was the supplier and design authority for the whole system. We captured the stakeholder requirements from the client's request for quotation and a site survey, designed and manufactured the hardware and firmware, installed and commissioned it, and provided the first year of support. A SciFlair project manager was the single point of contact, with acceptance signed off by the client's project manager.
built: Ceiling-mounted occupancy sensors, each covering about 5 m from a 2 m ceiling, with programmable time-outs of 10–30 minutes for lights and 15–30 minutes for air-conditioning
SciFlair controller boards with 8 inputs, 6 outputs and 10 A relays to switch each lighting circuit
Infrared transmitters that switch the existing ceiling-cassette air-conditioning units with no modification to the units
A wired RS485 network linking the controllers, with a status interface to the site's security management system
Fail-safe logic: manual switches remain the master, a failed module affects no other, and the system works without the site IT network
builtScope: In the main administration building alone: 121 air-conditioning units (100 indoor, 21 outdoor) and 45 lighting circuits across two floors.

delivery.title: Requirements traceability
delivery.text: Every requirement in the client's request for quotation was answered in a compliance matrix (fully, partially or not compliant, with reasons), forming the baseline for design and acceptance.

delivery.title: Stage plan
delivery.text: An eight-week plan from order to handover, with scope changes documented and justified through change control.

delivery.title: Verification
delivery.text: Controllers, sensors and transmitters were tested in our factory before shipping.

delivery.title: Decision gate: primary acceptance
delivery.text: A first stage installed five controllers and their sensors, tested and signed off by the client before the full rollout.

delivery.title: Validation and transition
delivery.text: Full installation, a signed site acceptance test in operational use, and handover with as-installed overlay drawings.

results.label: AC units controlled in the admin building

nextGen.title: What came next: the wireless Electricity Saver range
nextGen.text: Lessons from the plant led us to develop a wireless, battery-powered product line that installs in minutes: the S720 motion sensor (up to 5 years on two AAA batteries), the S710 air-conditioning controller with a built-in IR learner, and the S715 light controller for loads up to 2,000 W, all on an IEEE 802.15.4 mesh with up to 100 m range and a certified radio module.
